Micro E-mini S&P 500 (MES futures, Dec 2026): new plan.
Levels use the plan's prices.
If price trades into 7,520–7,530, the desk is bullish on the S&P 500 over the period to Thu 12 Nov, 07:00 ET. Invalidated if price moves below 7,480.
Why:
• Base case 52% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): the S&P 500 holds above 7,500 and extends the 9 Nov squeeze beyond the 7,581.97 post-event high within three sessions.
• Main alternative 38% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): a hot CPI seals a December Fed hike, the day-one squeeze fails and the S&P 500 falls back through 7,500 toward the old 7,446 ceiling.
• Mechanism: a global risk impulse, lower oil plus covering of an index short. Asia holds 7,556-7,567 and Nikkei futures rose 3.2%. the S&P 500 is a net transmitter in the connectedness row (+0.24).
• What is priced: drift +1.38 ATR from the 6 Nov close of 7,383.33 to the 7,561.65 capture; one-day move 1.81 volatility-normalised; 20-day mean 7,618.2 (z -0.44), 50-day 7,681.8 (z -1.10), 200-day 7,450.3 (z +0.33); 20-day range 7,300.5-7,792.4; ATR 128.9 at the 99.4th percentile; VIX closed 19.92 on 9 Nov, an implied daily move near 95 points; prior pricing AMBIGUOUS.
• Positioning: E-mini non-commercial net short 129,414, 6.5% of open interest, dated 3 Nov before the 5 Nov crash (a weak squeeze gauge); the negative GEX proxy dated 23 Oct means dealer hedging amplifies a break either way.
• Today's driver: mixed (oil, de-escalation and chips other than Nvidia against hike risk and the Nvidia probe).
• Reaction so far: the rally held into the close (7,562.9 against the 7,581.97 high), but on a mixed channel a day-one move is unconfirmed (4 Nov lesson), so continuation belongs beyond 7,581.97 and a test of that extreme is expected.
• Why this zone: pullback zone 7,520.00-7,530.00 at the first post-breakout base (9 Nov 11:00 ET H1 low 7,519.48, bar open 2026-11-09T16:00Z, known 2026-11-10T00:24:30.309Z; breakout zone 7,586.00-7,596.00 above the nearest resistance, the 9 Nov 15:00 ET H1 high of 7,581.97 (same evidence and clock).
• What confirms it: (1) the hold of the 7,445.67 breakout into the close in the the S&P 500 H1 and M15 bars; (2) the cross-asset risk impulse in the native-intraday frames (the Nasdaq 100 +4.13%, oil lower).
• Alternative mechanism: a hot CPI seals a December hike and the day-one squeeze fails; the Nvidia probe hits AI capex sentiment.; Crowd trade (G05 5): chasing the short-covering rally, wrong on a hot CPI or Nvidia news.

Analysis, not financial advice. Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.

Euro (EUR.USD spot): new plan.
Levels use the plan's prices.
If price trades into 1.1201–1.1205, the desk is bullish on EUR/USD over the period to Thu 12 Nov, 07:00 ET. Invalidated if price moves below 1.1182.
Why:
• Base case 55% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): EUR/USD holds above 1.1200 and extends the 9 Nov USD-weak move through the 1.1225 high within three sessions.
• Mechanism: a US-leg move, clear in the captured bars. the 20-day EUR/USD-DXY correlation is -0.966 (beta -1.09). Euro-area inflation at 4% and ECB December hike talk are optional local support.
• What is priced: drift +1.38 ATR from the 6 Nov close of 1.11398 to the 1.12197 capture; one-day move 2.18 volatility-normalised; 20-day mean 1.11934 (z +0.82), 50-day 1.12796, 200-day 1.15026 (z -1.60); 20-day range 1.11044-1.12731; prior pricing AMBIGUOUS; US 2-year yields about +3bp on 9 Nov; CPI consensus +0.3% headline and +0.2% core m/m.
• Positioning: EUR non-commercial net short 157,791 (COT as of 3 Nov, released 6 Nov), which covers above 1.1225 and 1.12348.
• Reaction so far: accepted.
• Why this zone: breakout zone 1.12270-1.12300 above the nearest resistance, the 9 Nov 15:00 ET H1 high of 1.12250 (same evidence and clock).
• What confirms it: (1) the same-session USD fall across DXY, GBP/USD and NZDUSD in the native-intraday and cc164 H1 bars; (2) the -0.966 20-day DXY correlation in the EUR/USD quant card; (3) the crowded EUR short in COT as of 3 Nov.
• Alternative mechanism: a hot core CPI that seals a December Fed hike and restores the NFP USD bid (DXY 102.032 to 102.36 on 6 Nov 08:00-09:00 ET).; Crowd trade (G05 5): chasing USD weakness into CPI, wrong on that print.

Analysis, not financial advice. Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.

Micro WTI crude oil (MCL futures, Dec 2026): new plan.
Levels use the plan's prices.
If price trades into 86.3–86.7, the desk is bearish on US crude oil (WTI) over the period to Thu 12 Nov, 07:00 ET. Invalidated if price moves above 88.35.
Why:
• Base case 55% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): WTI keeps unwinding its Iran risk premium, sells off from any retest of the broken 86.0-86.7 shelf and breaks below the 9 Nov low of 84.24 within three sessions.
• Main alternative 35% (Capital Chronicle model estimate): stalled US-Iran talks or Hormuz tanker incidents restore the supply premium and squeeze WTI back above 88.2.
• Mechanism: the supply-premium channel, clear for oil. The D1 bars fell from 104.04 (30 Oct high) to 84.237 (9 Nov low), each bounce failed (91.449 on 6 Nov and 90.464 on 9 Nov were sold), and 9 Nov opened at 89.50 and closed at 85.547, below the 5 Nov low of 86.02, on US-Iran deal hopes and the Hormuz framework report. WTI is a net receiver in the connectedness row and its 20-day correlation with the S&P 500 is -0.55.
• What is priced: drift -1.00 ATR from the 6 Nov close of 89.483 to the 85.584 capture; 5-day -2.62 ATR (-10.7%); 10-day -15.4%; 20-day mean 96.72 (z -2.09), 50-day 94.36 (z -1.87), 200-day 88.74; 20-day range 84.24-104.04; prior pricing AMBIGUOUS.
• Positioning: speculators net long 80,289, only 4.2% of 1,908,732 open interest (COT as of 3 Nov, before the fall from 95.8 to 84.2), modest fuel below 84.2; shorts cover above 88.2.
• Today's driver: clear, the Iran premium, and the D1 bars agree.
• Reaction so far: accepted; the 9 Nov close of 85.547 sits near the 84.237 low and below 86.02, and Asia steadies near 85.6.
• Why this zone: pullback zone 86.30-86.70 at the broken shelf of the 5 Nov D1 low 86.02 (bar open 2026-11-05T00:00Z) and the 4 Nov low 86.59; breakout zone 83.95-84.10 below the nearest support, the 9 Nov D1 low of 84.237 (bar open 2026-11-09T00:00Z); both known 2026-11-10T00:24:18.044Z.
• What confirms it: (1) the repeated bounce failures at 91.449 and 90.464 and the close below 86.02 in the D1 bars; (2) the -0.55 the S&P 500 correlation in the WTI quant card, consistent with a supply rather than a demand move.
• Alternative mechanism: stalled talks or Hormuz incidents restore the supply premium; which may be an escalation headline.
• Invalidation: a completed H1 close above 88.35, or official confirmation of strikes that disrupt supply or a Hormuz closure.

Analysis, not financial advice. Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.
